newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Banque Mediterranee doubles capital.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Banque Mediterranee doubles capital.

text.p: Banque de la Mediterranee, Lebanon's biggest bank, has more than doubled its capital to $212 million, Chairman Mustafa Razian said on Tuesday.
"We concluded another increase of capital at the end of last year which puts our capital at 330 billion Lebanese pounds which is about $212 million," Razian told Reuters in a telephone interview.
This compares with Banque Audi, which ranks second among Lebanese banks in terms of shareholders' equity with $63 million capital.

Before the increase Mediterranee's capital was $102 million, with a 14.1 percent market share among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks, according to Bilanbanques Liban 1996, a compilation of Lebanese banking data.

Razian said the $110 million capital increase came from 1996 profits, which totalled about $20 million, and from shareholder cash. The bank is 100 percent owned by Lebanon's Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri.
"This increase is in line with our policy to strengthen the capital base of the bank which stems from our belief that the bank's first asset is its capital," Razian said.
He told Reuters last October that his target was to increase Mediterranee's capital to $500 million by the year 2,000.
The bank's previous capital increase was in December 1995 to $102 million from about $47 million.
Lebanon's Al-Iktissad Wal-Amal (Economy and Business) magazine last year listed Mediterranee as 59th -- the highest Lebanese bank -- among the top 100 Arab banks in 1995. It was 80th in 1994.
Mediterranee has 24 branches in Lebanon and 531 employees, according to the Almanach of the Lebanese Banks Association.
